title: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness: Toggling 'Reasoning Mode' Made One Model 5x More Likely to Follow Its Own Mistakes
why_read: A hands-on benchmark measuring how faithfully different LLMs' visible reasoning steps actually drive their final answers, with a concrete methodology and numeric results.
analysis: The author formalizes an earlier anecdotal impression, that Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude respond differently to injected mid-reasoning errors, into an actual measured benchmark using the 'Adding Mistakes' intervention technique from Anthropic's 2023 chain-of-thought faithfulness research. The core question, whether a model's displayed reasoning genuinely drives its answer or is just a plausible-looking narration added afterward, is directly relevant to anyone relying on visible reasoning traces to trust or debug LLM outputs. Finding that toggling a 'reasoning mode' setting made one model five times more likely to blindly follow an injected mistake is a concrete, testable, and practically important result. This kind of grounded, methodologically transparent LLM behavior analysis is genuinely useful for engineers building on top of reasoning models.
